title: Falsifiable Hypothesis Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Classification activity in which learners decide whether each of eight illustrative electrical engineering research statements is falsifiable or not falsifiable. Statements appear in a fixed order with one attempt each; feedback gives Correct or the correct classification, the reason, and for a not-falsifiable statement the missing element. The run ends with a score out of 8 and whether the mastery threshold of 7 was met.

learningObjectives: Distinguish falsifiable hypotheses from statements that no experiment could contradict, among eight statements, with at least 7 of 8 classified correctly

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; correct and incorrect feedback uses a check mark or X and words as well as a blue or orange color; all text is 16 px or larger. At container widths under about 360 px the buttons wrap onto a second row and the drawing region shrinks by the same amount.

controls.label: Falsifiable
controls.purpose: Commits the answer Falsifiable for the current statement. Disabled after the single attempt.

controls.label: Not falsifiable
controls.purpose: Commits the answer Not falsifiable for the current statement. Disabled after the single attempt.

controls.label: Next / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after an answer is committed. Advances to the next statement, and after statement 8 shows the final score.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Forced binary classification with one attempt per item and immediate explanatory feedback naming the missing element
keyQuestions: Could any measurement show this to be wrong?
Does the statement name a measurable quantity?
Does it name a threshold or a direction and size of effect?
Does it name the conditions under which it is tested?
commonMisconceptions: A statement with a number in it is falsifiable
A confident, technical-sounding statement is a hypothesis
A statement that cannot fail is the strongest claim
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 statements classified correctly on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the checklist of properties is exploration and is not evidence
